## Goal

Two places claim to know the app's version and they disagree: the app factory
hardcodes `0.1.0`, the settings object carries `1.0.0`, and the health endpoint
reads the factory value - which is why the live service answers
`"version":"0.1.0"` while `render.yaml` (since t91) and the blueprint gate both
speak `1.0.0`. This card deletes the duplicate: one line in one file, so the
payload reports the configured version and `config.py` becomes the single source
of truth it was already meant to be.

### Recon correction (measured; the survey's shorthand is not executable)

The survey and the phase_14 recon both write the fix as
`version=settings.APP_VERSION`, "importing `settings` per the file's existing
import style". Measured: `app/config.py` exposes `get_settings()` (an
`@lru_cache` factory) and NO module-level `settings`. The literal edit was
applied and measured, not argued:

- `version=settings.APP_VERSION` with no new binding -> `NameError: name
  'settings' is not defined`; **15 collection errors**, the whole backend suite
  cannot even be collected (ac1/ac3 both RED, and the RED text names it).
- `version=settings.APP_VERSION` plus a new module-level `settings =
  get_settings()` -> ruff/mypy clean and the payload correct, but it invents a
  module-level alias evaluated at import time, grows the file to 133 lines, and
  diverges from the file's own `create_app()` style. ac1 REDs it (line-count
  leg).
- `version=get_settings().APP_VERSION` -> **the spelling this card pins**: one
  line, no new name, `create_app()` reads the same cached object the router and
  `telemetry.build_resource()` read, ruff and mypy clean, 302 tests GREEN.

The card pins ONE spelling so the builder cannot guess and the verifier cannot
grade on a moving standard. ac1's exact-transition leg is the fence that says so.

an extra product file always is.

## Constraints (hard)

- ZERO gate edits. `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` (318 entries, blob
  `a9f600be048a...`) is orchestrator-owned and this card has NO amendment to
  hand over. A card that "fixes" a gate is a FAIL even if the gate goes green;
  ac5's amendment-artifact leg and index-blob leg are the fences that catch it.
- Exactly ONE product line changes: `backend/app/main.py:81`, to
  `version=get_settings().APP_VERSION`. No line added, no line removed, no
  reordering, no comment added (ac1 compares line sets against the BASE blob, so
  an added line REDs even if another is deleted to compensate).
- No new import, no module-level `settings` binding, no `__version__` module, no
  `pyproject.toml` edit, no `VERSION` file, no changelog, no version BUMP -
  inventing a third version mechanism is the exact defect this card removes
  (measured: an untracked `backend/VERSION` REDs ac2; a `1.0.1` bump REDs ac2
  and ac3).
- `backend/app/config.py` is not touched: it is read, never edited (ac2 pins its
  blob and its `APP_VERSION: str = "1.0.0"` line).
- No test is weakened, skipped, deselected, renamed away from collection, or
  deleted (ac2 pins `test_health_api.py`'s blob, ac4 pins the three suite counts
  and REDs any skip/deselect marker in the summary).
- `openapi.yaml` is FROZEN (blob `684cd411cb46...`), `README.md` is FROZEN for
  this card (398 lines / `ca9343a8`; t94 and t96 are this milestone's only README
  single-writer cards), `render.yaml` keeps its post-t91 bytes (blob
  `c5e2553862dc...`), and `.github/**` stays t90's. Do not touch
  `docs/criteria/**`, `scripts/**`, `frontend/**`, or any other `backend/` file.
- The delta is single-file: `backend/app/main.py` is the only product file. t90
  (#96) is NOT merged and its `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` operator edit is
  ANCESTOR-owned - it may sit uncommitted in the work tree or arrive via a merged
  ancestor, but it may NEVER be committed on this card's branch.
- Do not close, comment on, or relabel any platform issue beyond what groom owns;
  the builder commits only `backend/app/main.py` plus its own card/handoff room.
- The live payload change (`0.1.0` -> `1.0.0` on
